questions.question: Write word equations for the reactions of magnesium with oxygen and iron with sulfur. List four observations that show a chemical reaction has taken place, and explain why the magnesium oxide weighs more than the magnesium.
questions.expected_answer: Magnesium + oxygen → magnesium oxide. Iron + sulfur → iron sulfide. Observations: a new substance with different properties forms; colour change (grey to white); light and heat given out; gas produced; a solid forming from solutions; the change is hard to reverse. Magnesium oxide weighs more because the magnesium atoms have combined with oxygen atoms from the air; the mass of the product is the mass of magnesium plus the mass of oxygen gained, since atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed.

questions.question: Magnesium and oxygen combine in a mass ratio of 3 : 2. Calculate the mass of oxygen needed and magnesium oxide formed from 12 g of magnesium. Explain what happens when 10 g of iron is heated with 4 g of sulfur, given that they combine in a ratio of 7 : 4.
questions.expected_answer: 12 g Mg × 2/3 = 8 g oxygen; 12 + 8 = 20 g magnesium oxide. Iron and sulfur: 4 g of sulfur needs 7 g of iron, so 7 g of iron reacts with all 4 g of sulfur to form 7 + 4 = 11 g of iron sulfide, and 10 − 7 = 3 g of iron is left over unreacted, because a compound forms only in its fixed ratio (law of constant composition); mass is conserved: 10 + 4 = 11 + 3 = 14 g.

questions.question: Describe how compounds are decomposed by heating and by electrolysis, using copper carbonate and water as examples, and give the tests for carbon dioxide, hydrogen and oxygen.
questions.expected_answer: Thermal decomposition: copper carbonate (green) is heated strongly → copper oxide (black) + carbon dioxide. Electrolysis: an electric current is passed through water with a little dilute acid or sodium sulfate using two electrodes; water → hydrogen + oxygen, with hydrogen at the negative electrode (cathode) and oxygen at the positive electrode (anode), in a 2 : 1 volume ratio. Tests: carbon dioxide turns limewater milky; hydrogen burns with a squeaky pop when a lighted splint is held to it; oxygen relights a glowing splint.
